sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cynan is a hero of Welsh legend. He is the brother-in-law of a half-historical king named Maxen. Cynan helps Maxen rise to rule as emperor of the western Roman lands. For that service he gains control of Brittany. There he silences the local women by removing their tongues. He acts to guard his own warriors' Welsh speech from any rival. Like Maxen, Cynan seems invented for a political end. He is tied to statecraft, not to worship or ritual.
